Built-in ImageGen mode. Existing skitter walking atlas used as identity/style reference.

Initial generation prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production RGBA sprite atlas for a pixel-style hack-and-slash RPG with an orthographic 45-degree elevated camera. Image 1 is a STYLE AND CREATURE IDENTITY REFERENCE ONLY, not an edit target. Preserve this same low armored skitter beetle: blue-grey segmented carapace, cream/bone horn edges and curved mandibles, six dark articulated legs, small amber eyes. Preserve the crunchy pixel edges, restrained texture, warm highlights and neutral shadow colors of the reference. No floor, no cast shadow, no backdrop, no UI, no words, no grid lines, no letters, no borders, no numbers, no particles, no speed streaks. Truly transparent alpha background. Each pose must be completely separated by generous transparent gutters. Keep the body scale and ground contact origin constant across each row. Never translate the whole creature forward between poses; animation happens in place. Only one creature per cell. Keep all legs and horns connected to the body, including death poses. Render a clean rectangular sheet with evenly spaced rows and columns. Draw sprites small, around 55 percent of cell width and 60 percent of cell height, with at least 25 percent total transparent side padding. Five directional rows from top to bottom: South (front toward viewer), Southeast (front-right diagonally), East (profile facing RIGHT), Northeast (rear-right diagonally), North (back away from viewer). All five rows use the same elevated camera, not a top-down overhead sketch. Do not turn the E or SE rows left. Reuse exactly the same anatomy, shell segments and horn arrangement in all poses. Produce exactly FIVE ROWS by FOUR COLUMNS, 20 sprites total. Read each row left to right as one attack sequence: column 1 alert preparation, planted rear legs and raised forelegs; column 2 deep telegraph windup, shell lowered and mandibles wide open with front claws drawn back; column 3 HIT/CONTACT, sharp forward mandible snap and foreclaw strike, shell thrusts but body's ground origin stays in the same cell position; column 4 post-hit recovery with mandibles closing and front legs settling toward the original standing stance. Clearly distinguish preparation, loaded windup, contact and recovery. Contact faces precisely the row direction. Final pose should bridge back to the reference walking posture. Do not add a projectile or sword. Keep every sprite inside its own equally sized cell. Make a broad rectangular atlas with five clearly aligned rows.

Final correction prompt:
Edit target: the supplied transparent five-row four-column skitter attack atlas. Make exactly ONE local correction. The second sprite in the top row (South loaded windup, row 1 column 2) has turned diagonally. Redraw ONLY this sprite as a fully FRONT-FACING South view, bilaterally symmetric like the first and third sprites of the top row: equal visible eyes on both sides, central forward mandibles, carapace axis vertical, equal left/right foreshortening. Keep its loaded crouched telegraph with raised foreclaws and open mandibles, its existing body size, its original centered ground origin and its cell gutters. Preserve the other 19 sprites, every row/column placement, carapace identity, pixel edges, palette and alpha transparency. Do not touch other cells, add any background, text, shadow or decoration. Output the same transparent atlas.
